We have about five minutes left. What questions do you have for me?
Thank you. What do the students who do well in the first year have in common?
Mostly, they ask for help early. The ones who struggle are usually the ones who try to do everything alone.
What makes you say that? Is it something you see in the learning teams?
Exactly. A student who never asks a question in week two is usually in trouble by week ten.
That is very insightful. Who decides which team each student joins?
The program office does. We never put two people from the same industry in one team, so you would probably be the only engineer.
Then let me dig deeper. How have engineers done in teams like that, and what did they find hardest?

Who would I work with most closely?

At the end of every interview, I ask the candidate if he has any questions for me, and it is not a formality. It is the last part of the evaluation. The weakest answer is no. The second weakest is a generic question that anybody could answer from our website, like how long the program is. A good question shows me that you did your homework, and that you are already imagining yourself in the program. The best candidates do one more thing. They listen to my answer and ask a follow-up question. That is rare, and it tells me something important: that this person will be curious in the classroom, not only in the interview. Two good questions with a follow-up are worth more than ten questions from a list.

In my interview, when they asked me if I had any questions, I asked the one I really cared about. I said: my company is a family business, and I will be away one week in every six. What do the students who run family companies do to keep things going while they are here? The interviewer smiled and said that nobody had asked her that before. She told me about two alumni who had set up a weekly call with their deputies, and then she asked me who my deputy would be. I did not have an answer. That question was the most useful thing I took from the whole day. By the time the program started, I had prepared somebody for the job.
